analysis.title: "Déjà Vu": JPMorgan Finds 3.8GW Of Malaysia's Data Center Pipeline Tied To Chinese Operators As Washington Moves To Shut The Backdoor
key_insights: JPMorgan's Malaysia data center tracker puts the pipeline at about 12.7GW, versus 5.9GW tracked in 2025. Of that, 1.3GW is live, 2.2GW is under construction, 4.0GW is committed and 5.2GW is early-stage. About 72% has not broken ground.

JPMorgan's tracker identifies about 3.8GW of capacity associated with Chinese data center operators, about 25% of the pipeline. The tracker maps operators rather than tenants, so it excludes Chinese tenants leasing from non-Chinese colocation providers (Yondr, BDC, K2). The article says 3.8GW over 12.7GW is 30%, not 25%, and that real Chinese end-demand exposure is higher than the headline.

US export controls govern where a chip is shipped, not who rents compute on it. A Chinese AI lab can therefore lease Blackwell capacity in Johor legally. Goldman's Asia economics team called this 'export-control arbitrage' in a September note.

Per The Information, BIS is in the final stages of a rule that would add Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, Brazil, Norway and South Africa to the license list for chips at or above Blackwell, with importers naming the end user. It could land this month. The WSJ reports Commerce is weighing new export rules and licensing for the four Southeast Asian countries. Both parties are trying to attach chip curbs to the defense bill (NDAA).

The Information puts the value of Nvidia chips that moved through Megaspeed and Speedmatrix at no less than $7.5B. Per Bloomberg, Nvidia's own tally to the US government missed 50,000 chips. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. Epoch AI estimates about 275,000 Nvidia accelerators were imported into Malaysia in 2024-2025.

JPMorgan sees relatively low direct exposure for Gamuda (GAM) and Sunway Construction (SCGB), because most of their data center clients are Western hyperscalers building for their own use. JPM counts 24 hyperscaler packages in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan worth 1,554MW and RM46.6B, of which 14 packages (828MW, RM24.8B) are not yet awarded. Gamuda has about 15% of its orderbook in data centers. For SunCon, each RM1B of data center wins moves FY27/28 earnings by 3-4%.

JPMorgan's defense of YTL Power: GPU procurement sits with tenants, contracts are long-dated with bank guarantees, and the integrated land, power and data center position lets it target US tenants. YTL's 150MW of live capacity is split evenly between US and non-US customers. Tenaga has five-year take-or-pay supply agreements. NationGate's Nvidia GPU assembly lasted about three quarters, and JPM removed GPU revenue from forecasts at end-2025.

All five stocks in the JPM note are rated Overweight. Price targets sit 26% to 64% above Thursday's close (YTL Power target RM7.20 versus RM4.40). YTL Power fell 8% Thursday and is down about 26% since end-September. Gamuda fell 3% Friday. SunCon trades at 20x forward earnings versus a 10-year average of 17x, and Gamuda at 18x versus 15x.

Precedent: after the January 2025 AI diffusion rule, YTL Power fell 13% and Gamuda 9% in two weeks. JPM cut Sunway Construction and YTL Power to Underweight and Gamuda to Neutral. The rule was later scrapped and SunCon more than doubled. This time the rule comes from Trump's own Commerce Department and Congress wants a tougher one.

Goldman's 'Exports and Beyond' note expects ASEAN data center capacity to quadruple in five years, with Johor the largest regional hub by 2030. Malaysia has about 1.3GW live, more than Singapore, Korea or Hong Kong. Data center construction adds an average 30bps a year to Malaysian GDP in 2026-2028, with about 36bps next year. AI contributes 3.4 points of Malaysia's 5.2% growth this year, of which 2.8 points is tech hardware exports. The data center slice (0.2 points construction plus 0.4 points ICT services exports) is about 0.6 points.

Malaysia's ICT services balance swung from a deficit of 20bps of GDP to a surplus of 30bps between Q2 2025 and Q2 2026. The article reads this as foreigners renting compute located in Malaysia. Malaysia's net diesel generator imports ran more than $200M above their 2018-22 average.

Malaysia has approved RM385.7B ($95B) of data center investment since 2021, and only 55 of 117 approved projects are operating. Trade Minister Johari Abdul Ghani said the government is drafting a law requiring data centers to disclose operators, locations, power use and GPU counts. A tenant can bring AI chips in without a permit, and only exports have required a license since July 2025.

Morgan Stanley's Nov 2 note estimated about 15GW of the US data center power shortfall spills to Asia, with Malaysia taking the largest share at 4GW. The article argues US hyperscalers could backfill Chinese capacity, but every Blackwell headed to Malaysia would still need a US license, which slows deployment.

Reported precursors: Oracle cancelled a $7B chip-leasing deal with Tencent across its Southeast Asian data centers after a visit from Trump officials, and Nvidia told cloud customers 51% of services must go to non-Chinese clients. Nov 18 is the date for a closed-door House committee briefing on Jensen Huang's dealings with Alice Huang. The article says Huang is out at Nvidia.

market_movers.rationale: JPM rates YTL Power Overweight with a RM7.20 target versus RM4.40 close. It says tenants procure the GPUs, contracts are long-dated and bank-guaranteed, and it can target US tenants for future capacity.
JPM rates Gamuda Overweight and sees low direct exposure. About 15% of its orderbook is data centers and its client is a US hyperscaler.
JPM rates Sunway Construction Overweight. Each RM1B of data center wins moves FY27/28 earnings by 3-4%. Most of its clients are hyperscalers building for their own use.
JPM rates Tenaga Nasional Overweight, citing five-year take-or-pay supply agreements.
JPM rates NationGate Overweight. It removed GPU revenue from forecasts at end-2025, and licensing risk sits with exporters, not contract manufacturers.

sector_views.rationale: JPM sees low direct exposure for its covered stocks and says committed investments provide support. The article's author disagrees and expects the pipeline to shrink.
Goldman expects ASEAN capacity to quadruple in five years, driven by power constraints in tier-1 markets and export-control arbitrage.

risk_factors: A US rule covering remote access or existing capacity, not just shipments, would hit Chinese tenants already in Malaysia.
72% of Malaysia's pipeline has not broken ground, and 41% is early-stage.
The 828MW of unawarded hyperscaler packages could slip, which would show first in Gamuda and SunCon orderbooks.
JPM says a change in customers' investment plans or timelines would hit all contractors, even without direct restrictions.
Goldman warns that a moderation in hyperscaler capex would hurt ASEAN growth, citing higher financing costs, ROI scrutiny or slower AI adoption.
US licensing delays could slow US hyperscaler backfill of Chinese capacity.
geopolitical: US Commerce and BIS are preparing export license requirements for chips at or above Blackwell for Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, Brazil, Norway and South Africa.
Congress is trying to attach chip-control bills, including mandatory location tracking, to the NDAA.
Megaspeed and Speedmatrix are accused of diverting Nvidia chips to China. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.
Malaysia is drafting a data center disclosure law. The trade minister saw no legal basis to investigate Speedmatrix, and the PM says there is no sign chips left the country.
A House committee closed-door briefing on Huang's dealings with Alice Huang is set for Nov 18.
Oracle cancelled a $7B Tencent chip-leasing deal after a visit from Trump officials.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees low direct exposure for its covered stocks. Hyperscaler clients build for their own use, contracts are long-dated and bank-guaranteed, and committed investment provides support. Morgan Stanley sees 4GW of US demand spilling to Malaysia, which could backfill Chinese capacity.
tension_points.bear_case: The pipeline is 72% unbuilt and at least 25% tied to Chinese operators, with more through tenants. A Commerce rule would require US licenses for every Blackwell shipped to Malaysia, slowing builds. Stocks already fell, with YTL Power down about 26% since September.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Commerce publishing a rule that covers remote access to existing capacity, not just shipments, or slippage in the unawarded 828MW of hyperscaler packages.

theme_stances.key_argument: A pipeline that is 72% unbuilt and at least a quarter Chinese by operator is likely to shrink as US controls tighten.
